_readme: Partner romance arcs: one list of beats per partner key (from characters.json). A beat fires every few weeks once her trust is high enough; the last beat makes her Sam's lover.
Beat: title, scene (image scene: sam_date, shower, walkin, casual, portrait, bath, or final = her private scene with Sam), text, choices.
Choice: label plus effects. t/m/l = trust/mood/lewdness change. res = result text ({N} = her name). hold:true = the beat comes back later instead of advancing.
Extra effects: gold (negative = cost; add cantAfford:{...} for when Sam is short), sam:{strength:1} (Sam stat), energy:"full", health:20, grow:{service:6} (her skill).
Conditions: if:{lewd:40} (her stat at least that; also works for trust, mood) uses this choice's effects, otherwise the ones under else:{...}.
image (optional): {comp, setting, sam, towel} a picture for that beat instead of the generic scene. The scene key still decides bath/walk-in handling.

kaede.title: Two Stolen Bottles
kaede.text: Kaede hauls Sam up the ladder to the roof of the Lantern with two bottles of wine she very obviously did not pay for, the glass still cold and sweating from the cellar. The tiles hold the day's warmth, chimney smoke drifts past the stars, and her copper tail thumps the roof behind her. "Back in my party, nobody ever had my back. Then this skinny guy in a hoodie jumps in front of a goblin for me." She bumps his shoulder with hers. "Idiot." She doesn't move away, and the tail curls around his ankle.

choices.label: Stay on the roof with her
choices.res: Sam finds the bottle in his hand somehow empty and the stars somehow lower. Kaede's tail never unwinds from his ankle, and neither of them points it out.

choices.label: Pass the conversation back to her wine
choices.res: {N} snorts into the bottle and lets him off the hook. Her tail still sneaks one lazy swish against his leg as they climb down.

image.comp: sitting on a rooftop at night bumping shoulders with him, holding a wine bottle, fox tail swishing
image.setting: tiled rooftop over a fantasy town at night, stars, chimney smoke

kaede.title: Wrong Door
kaede.text: Sam shoulders open the washroom door and finds Kaede mid-towel, steam curling off her sun-kissed skin, the thin scar on her shoulder pink from the heat. Every single hair on her tail stands straight up like a startled bottlebrush. For one long second the only sound is a dripping tap and Sam's brain emptying itself of all vocabulary.

choices.label: Apologize and bolt
choices.res: Kaede laughs about it for ten straight minutes. Through the door. Loudly enough that the whole corridor learns what happened, and at dinner she toasts him with a spoon.

choices.label: Compliment her
choices.res: She grins, tail slowly settling, and doesn't bother holding the towel very hard. "Smooth, boss. Real smooth." The warmth in her voice outlasts the steam.

else.res: "GET OUT." The towel hits him square in the face, still warm and smelling of her soap, and the door slams hard enough to rattle the hinges.

choices.label: Stand there like an idiot
choices.res: "Take a picture, it lasts longer." Sam has no idea how she knows that phrase, but she is smirking when she says it, tail fluffed with pride rather than panic.

image.comp: frozen mid-towel in a washroom doorway, every hair on her fox tail standing straight up, wide-eyed
image.setting: steamy wooden washroom

kaede.title: Tail Says Otherwise
kaede.text: Kaede turns up at Sam's door with a bandaged hand and a bright grin, claiming she got hurt sparring "for fun." The knuckles under the linen are split and puffy, and she smells of liniment and sawdust. She sits on the edge of his bed while he unwinds and re-wraps it with clumsy care, and her tail keeps brushing his arm, back and forth, warm and soft. Neither of them mentions it.

choices.label: Finish the bandage slowly
choices.res: He takes his time over the knot, and she lets him, eyes on his hands instead of the wall. Her tail stops pretending it's accidental.

choices.label: Tie it off and tease her about sparring
choices.res: "For fun," Sam repeats, deadpan. {N} flicks his ear for it, but her laugh is soft and she stays seated a minute longer than she needs to.

image.comp: sitting on a kitchen table while he bandages her hand, grinning, fox tail brushing his arm
image.setting: inn kitchen at night, a first-aid kit

kaede.title: The Old Party
kaede.text: Kaede's old party leader turns up at the bar in dungeon-stained leathers, trailing the smell of rain and old smoke. He has a new contract, a deep dungeon and a spot for her, if she wants it. The common room goes quiet. Kaede doesn't look at him; she looks at Sam, ears pinned flat, and waits with her fingers drumming on the counter.

choices.label: "Go, if it's what you want."
choices.res: She stays. Later she grumbles into her cup: "You weren't supposed to make it easy." But she sits close all night.

choices.label: "Stay. Please."
choices.res: Kaede turns the leader down without even looking at him, and the ex-captain leaves with his ears burning. Her tail slaps Sam's leg twice under the bar, hard, happy.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.res: She leaves for two days without a word. When she comes back, she doesn't mention it. Neither does he. It sits between them for a while, like a bill nobody wants to read.

image.comp: standing at a bar between him and a rugged adventurer in armor, arms crossed, looking at him and waiting
image.setting: busy tavern bar, adventurers at tables

kaede.title: Rooftops
kaede.text: Kaede teaches Sam to run the rooftops of Hollowmere at night, hopping slate to slate in the moonlight as though gravity were a polite suggestion. Sam, in his grey hoodie and traveler's cloak, is very, very bad at it. He windmills across a gap, clings to a chimney, and apologizes to a pigeon. Kaede crouches on the ridgeline above, hands on her knees, wheezing with laughter.

choices.label: Keep trying
choices.res: By the end of the night he makes one jump cleanly. She cheers loud enough to wake the whole street, and a shutter bangs open below them. Neither cares.

choices.label: Fake a sprained ankle so she carries you
choices.res: She sees right through it, ears twitching with delight. She carries him anyway, the whole way home, over her shoulder and grumbling that he weighs nothing.

image.comp: leaping across rooftops at night, laughing back at the man clinging to a chimney
image.setting: moonlit rooftops of a fantasy town

kaede.title: Copper Fox, Kept
kaede.text: After closing, Kaede corners Sam in the kitchen, where the stove is still ticking as it cools and one lamp burns low. She drums her fingers on the table, stops, starts again. "I'm bad at this, so I'll just say it. I'm not going anywhere. Not for the money. For you." Her ears are bright red to the tips and her tail won't stop wagging. She takes his hand and leads him upstairs, and the door closes behind them.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: {N} nods too fast. "I can wait. Don't make it too long." Her tail droops, then perks up again, stubborn.

yui.title: Almost Coffee
yui.text: Yui finds Sam on the back steps at dusk with two cups of something that is almost, but not quite, coffee. It smells of burnt barley, and they both pull the same face at the first sip. They talk about home for hours: trains, convenience stores, the vending machine on the 4th floor that only ever ate her coins. She pushes her glasses up, twice, and then she cries a little. So does he.

choices.label: Sit with her until the cups go cold
choices.res: They stay there until the cups are cold and the lanterns are lit, shoulders touching, saying the names of train stations like prayers. She files the evening under "keep."

choices.label: Pass her a napkin and a joke
choices.res: Sam offers a napkin and a terrible vending machine joke. {N} laughs wetly, pushes up her glasses, and leans just a little against the step rail closer to him.

image.comp: sitting on back steps with him holding two steaming cups, laughing about home
image.setting: back steps of an inn at night, lanterns, stars

yui.title: Bath Time Budget Meeting
yui.text: Hunting for the ledger, Yui walks straight into the washroom while Sam is in the tub, a cloud of steam rolling past her glasses until they fog completely. She does not leave. She stares fixedly at the ceiling. Then the floor. Then the ceiling again, clutching the account book to her chest like a shield, her ears the color of boiled shrimp.

choices.label: "Could you pass me a towel?"
choices.res: She throws it directly at his face and flees, the account book forgotten on the stool. He finds a neat sticky note inside: "Variance: 1 towel."

choices.label: Act completely casual
choices.res: She stammers through the entire weekly budget review, right there, without once looking down, glasses fogged, voice cracking on "depreciation." It's honestly impressive. He approves every line item.

choices.label: Yell
choices.res: She flees, mortified, glasses clattering on the tiles, and avoids him for three days, sliding reports under his door instead of speaking.

image.comp: standing in a washroom doorway clutching a ledger, staring fixedly at the ceiling, bright red
image.setting: steamy wooden washroom, a man in the tub off-frame

yui.title: Instant Ramen, Reconstructed
yui.text: Yui reveals she's been "recreating" instant ramen in the kitchen for a month. The broth is a pale, apologetic grey, and the noodles have the texture of wet rope. It is terrible. They eat all of it anyway, passing one chipped bowl back and forth. "Remember when you covered my shift that time?" she asks, eyes on the steam. "I liked you before the truck, you know."

choices.label: Tell her you liked her too, then finish the bowl
choices.res: He tells her, a little clumsily, and she covers her face with the cup. They scrape the bowl clean. She says it's the best ramen she's ever made, and for once she is not lying about it.

choices.label: Declare it a triumph of accounting
choices.res: "Best ramen in the realm," Sam says, which is technically true. {N} laughs, tucks her hair behind her ear, and doesn't take back what she said.

image.comp: eating a terrible bowl of homemade ramen with him at a kitchen table, both laughing
image.setting: small inn kitchen at night, pots and steam

yui.title: The Way Home
yui.text: A traveling mage claims he can send otherworlders home. Yui shows Sam the flyer with shaking hands, the ink smeared where she's held it too long. It smells of cheap incense. She stands in the doorway of the office and won't come inside. "If it's real... would you go?"

choices.label: "I'd stay. This is home now."
choices.res: She lets out a breath she's been holding for a week, shoulders dropping an inch, and straightens the flyer into a neat square before putting it away.

choices.label: "I don't know."
choices.res: Honest. It still hurts. She nods, pushes her glasses up, and files the flyer in a drawer. She doesn't bring it up again.

choices.label: "Only if you came with me."
choices.res: She laughs and wipes her eyes under her glasses. (The mage turns out to be a fraud. Neither of them is disappointed.)

image.comp: holding a crumpled flyer with shaking hands, looking up at him with teary eyes
image.setting: quiet office at dusk

yui.title: Festival Night
yui.text: Yui drags Sam to the harvest festival, all lantern strings and fried dough, and wins him a prize at the ring toss: a deeply ugly stuffed wyvern with mismatched button eyes. She insists he carry it all night. People stare. She enjoys that more than she'll admit, her cheeks pink with cider and delight.

choices.label: Wear it like a hat, proudly
choices.res: She laughs so hard she has to sit down on a barrel, glasses crooked. For the rest of the night, strangers toast the hat.

choices.label: Win her one back
choices.res: It takes eleven tries, a lot of coins and a vendor's pity. She keeps the slightly-less-ugly griffin on her desk forever, between the stapler and the abacus.

image.comp: at a harvest festival handing him an ugly stuffed wyvern prize, triumphant grin
image.setting: harvest festival at night, game stalls, paper lanterns

yui.title: Second Chance
yui.text: Yui takes Sam's hand under the table during the staff meeting and doesn't let go, her thumb tracing the inside of his wrist while she reads out the quarterly figures in a perfectly level voice. Afterward, in the empty office, the lamp low, ledgers stacked behind her: "Second life. Second chance. I'm not wasting this one being shy." She kisses him, glasses bumping his nose, and pulls him toward her room.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: {N} nods and squeezes his hand once. "I can wait. Don't make it too long." She pushes up her glasses and goes back to her columns, smiling.

nerys.title: Inconvenient Feelings
nerys.text: Nerys complains, at length, that the contract makes her feel it when Sam is sad, a cold little ache under her ribs like a clause she never wrote. "It's very inconvenient. Stop being sad." Her tail lashes the cushion in irritation. Then she sits down next to him on the lounge sofa, thigh to thigh, wings folded tight, and stays until he isn't.

choices.label: Let her sit there and stay quiet
choices.res: They sit in silence long enough for the candles to gutter. She keeps muttering that she's only doing this for her own comfort. Her tail wraps lightly around his ankle.

choices.label: Tell her sadness is non-negotiable
choices.res: "Read the fine print," Sam says. {N} narrows her magenta eyes, sniffs, and stays exactly where she is, tail twitching in what might be amusement.

image.comp: sitting very close to him on a sofa, arms crossed, sulking, wings folded, pretending not to care
image.setting: dim lounge late at night

nerys.title: Oops
nerys.text: Sam opens the washroom door to find Nerys lounging in the tub, steam clinging to her violet hair, bat wings draped over the rim, very obviously waiting. "Oops," she says, not moving at all, one slender tail tip dipping in the water to draw lazy circles.

choices.label: Leave politely
choices.res: She looks almost disappointed. Almost. The tail tip stills, then goes back to circles as the door shuts, unmistakably sulky.

choices.label: Call her bluff and sit down on the stool
choices.res: For once, SHE is the one who goes red, the blue-tinted skin of her cheeks darkening to plum. She recovers quickly. Mostly. Her wings give her away with a small, flustered rustle.

choices.label: Toss her a towel
choices.res: She catches it with her tail and drapes it over his head instead. "Amateur," she says, but she is smiling at the water.

image.comp: lounging in a bathtub, very obviously waiting, smirking at the viewer, not moving at all
image.setting: steamy wooden washroom, candles

nerys.title: Research Material
nerys.text: Sam finds Nerys reading a romance novel in the lounge, curled into a cushion with her horns tilted toward the lamp and her tail beating time behind her. She hides it in a panic, wings snapping shut, then throws a pillow at him. Later he finds it on his bed with a page dog-eared and a note in her sharp, looping hand: "For research."

choices.label: Read the dog-eared page and find her
choices.res: The page is, frankly, upsetting for a man of his experience. He finds her anyway and says nothing; she studies the ceiling with enormous interest, tail curling round the chair leg.

choices.label: Return it with a thoughtful review
choices.res: He returns it with a detailed critique of the pacing, as is tradition. {N} looks mortified, then argues about the ending until midnight.

image.comp: hiding a romance novel behind her back in a panic, throwing a pillow, flustered
image.setting: plush lounge, cushions everywhere

nerys.title: Leash
nerys.text: A demon noble mocks Nerys in front of the whole lounge for being "leashed to a human," his smile smooth as polished brass. She laughs it off, chin high, one wing flicking. That night, she snaps at Sam over nothing at all: a misplaced quill, a draft, the way he breathes. The contract hums uncomfortably between them.

choices.label: Defend her, publicly, the next day
choices.res: Sam has the demon noble thrown out, politely and with witnesses. Nerys pretends not to care. Her tail gives her away, wrapped around his wrist for the rest of the evening.

choices.label: Let her handle it
choices.res: She does, loudly, in three languages and with a surprising amount of cutlery. Then she sulks for days, wings drawn up around her like a cloak.

choices.label: Offer to break the contract
choices.res: She goes very still. "You want me gone?" Her voice is dangerously even. It takes him a long, miserable hour to fix that, and a promise he doesn't intend to break.

image.comp: laughing off a sneering demon noble in a lounge, tight forced smile, tail lashing
image.setting: velvet lounge full of guests, red lamplight

nerys.title: Night Market
nerys.text: Nerys drags Sam to the Underdistrict night market, all red lanterns and sizzling oil, and buys him every cursed snack she can find: glowing skewers, black dumplings, something still twitching in a paper cone. She watches with the fixed attention of a woman collecting evidence. Her tail is curled around his sleeve so he can't get lost.

choices.label: Eat everything she hands you
choices.res: One of them makes his ears glow for an hour, and strangers ask for directions to his face. She has never been happier, and tells him so by laughing until she has to lean on him.

choices.label: Buy her a hair ribbon
choices.res: She acts unimpressed, holding the ribbon between two claws like evidence. She wears it every day after, tied in her violet hair or around the base of her horn.

image.comp: holding out a skewer of strange glowing snacks to him at a night market, delighted grin
image.setting: underground night market, glowing stalls, crowds

nerys.title: Clause Kept
nerys.text: A demon scholar in ink-black robes offers to dissolve the contract, paperwork spread on the table with a flourish. Nerys tears it up in front of him, every page. "I'll keep it," she tells Sam afterward, in the empty lounge, looking anywhere but at him: the candles, the ceiling, her own claws. "I've grown... attached." Then she looks at him, and stops pretending.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: {N} lifts one eyebrow. "I can wait. Don't make it too long." Her tail flicks once, a clause left open, and she leaves the torn paper on his desk.

elowen.title: Bedside Manner
elowen.text: Elowen insists on a "check-up" and spends most of it nervously talking about herbs, rosemary in her braid, fingers pressed to his pulse a few seconds longer than the instructions require. The room smells of chamomile and lamp oil. At the end she admits she's never been this far from home, and that Sam makes it feel less far.

choices.label: Tell her the distance feels shorter to him too
choices.res: She keeps her fingers on his wrist and doesn't count anything. The tea goes cold between them, and neither says what the silence is for.

choices.label: Offer to be her patient any time
choices.res: "Any time," Sam says. {N} hides behind her sleeve, ears pink, and writes "weekly" in her notes before he can see it.

image.comp: pressing a stethoscope-like charm to his chest, nervously babbling about herbs
image.setting: small infirmary with herbs drying from the rafters

elowen.title: Tea Service
elowen.text: Elowen brings herbal tea to Sam's room at exactly the moment he's changing, the tray balanced carefully in both hands, a little steam rising off the pot. She sees. The tray hits the floor with a crash of porcelain, and the smell of mint and lemon balm rises from the rug. Sam stands frozen with one arm in a sleeve, and neither of them breathes.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.res: She laughs too, eventually, from behind both hands, shoulders shaking. They pick up the shards together, not quite looking up.

choices.label: Apologize profusely
choices.res: They both apologize to each other for ten minutes, bowing in turn like two clockwork birds, and the broken teapot is never mentioned again.

choices.label: "You're a healer. You've seen it all, right?"
choices.res: "Not... all," she says faintly, fanning her flushed face with a hand.

else.res: She turns red to the tips of her pointed ears and mutters something about anatomy textbooks, then kneels very fast to gather the shattered cups.

image.comp: dropping a tea tray in a doorway, hands over her face, peeking through her fingers
image.setting: small bedroom, spilled tea on the floor

elowen.title: Flower Crowns
elowen.text: They go flower-picking outside the walls "for medicine," a basket on Elowen's arm and the smell of crushed clover under their boots. Somewhere in the second hour the herb list is forgotten. Elowen weaves Sam a flower crown with quick, careful fingers. He makes a terrible one back, lopsided and shedding petals. She wears it all day.

choices.label: Wear her crown home
choices.res: He wears hers all the way back through the gate, pollen on his collar, and doesn't mind the guards' stares. She walks half a step closer than usual.

choices.label: Tell her the lopsided one suits her
choices.res: "It suits you," Sam says of his own wreck. {N} adjusts it on her braid with immense seriousness and says it is the finest crown in Hollowmere.

image.comp: placing a flower crown on his head in a meadow, holding the lopsided one he made her
image.setting: wildflower meadow outside town walls, sunny afternoon

elowen.title: Burnout
elowen.text: Elowen has been healing the dock workers for free, every night, for weeks, coming home with salt on her hem and shadows under her green eyes. Today she collapses in the kitchen mid-sentence about willow bark. Her rosemary sprig has come loose from her braid, and her hands are cold.

choices.label: Scold her
choices.res: She cries. Not because he's wrong. The rosemary stays on the floor where it fell, and she doesn't speak to him until morning.

choices.label: Take care of her for a day
choices.res: Sam makes soup (badly), reads to her (badly, doing the voices), and doesn't leave her side. She sleeps for fourteen hours, one hand curled in his sleeve.

choices.label: Fund a free clinic night (150g)
choices.res: One night a week, with help from the apothecary's apprentices. She hugs him so hard his ribs creak, and presses her damp face against his hoodie.

cantAfford.res: You can't afford it. She thanks you for trying.

image.comp: collapsed against kitchen cabinets, exhausted, healer's satchel spilled, the man kneeling beside her
image.setting: inn kitchen at night

elowen.title: Starlight
elowen.text: Elowen takes Sam to a hill outside town on a cloudless night, the grass cool and damp, and names the constellations of her homeland, one by one, in the soft old language of the cedar glade. Her finger traces lines across the dark. Her voice grows steadier with every name, and further away.

choices.label: Listen to every single one
choices.res: There are a lot of them. He doesn't mind. By the last one her head is on his shoulder, and she's stopped pointing.

choices.label: Make up a constellation for her
choices.res: "The Clumsy Healer." She shoves him. She uses the name forever, and writes it into the margins of her star chart in tiny, careful script.

image.comp: pointing up at the night sky from a hilltop, naming constellations, the man beside her
image.setting: grassy hilltop at night, sweeping starry sky

elowen.title: Long-Lived
elowen.text: Elowen kisses Sam first, very quickly, in the herb garden after dusk with moths circling the lamp, then hides her face in his shirt. "Elves live a long time," she mumbles into the grey cotton. "I'd like to spend some of it with you." Her braid smells of rosemary and rain. She doesn't let go of his hand all the way to her room.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: {N} nods against his chest, embarrassed and relieved. "I can wait. Don't make it too long." She's still holding his sleeve.

adelheid.title: Poison Taster
adelheid.text: Adelheid insists on tasting all of Sam's food for poison. Every meal, spoon first, her steel-blue eyes narrowed and the scar through her eyebrow pulled tight with solemnity. Soup, bread, a suspicious pear. She eventually admits, stiffly, over the last bite of his dinner, that she has started looking forward to dinner time.

choices.label: Ask her to stay for the whole meal
choices.res: She sits across from him in her armor, straight-backed, and eats a whole meal as a guest instead of a guard for the first time. She is very bad at it.

choices.label: Tell her she's allowed to finish the pear
choices.res: "Strictly for safety," Sam says, handing her the pear. {N} accepts it as a sacred duty, and eats it in tiny, reverent bites.

image.comp: in armor tasting food from his plate with great seriousness, napkin tucked in
image.setting: inn dining room at dinner time

adelheid.title: Rain Barrel
adelheid.text: Sam cuts through the training yard and finds Adelheid washing off after practice at the rain barrel, cold water streaming down her scarred shoulders, her short platinum hair plastered flat. She snaps to attention. With the hand holding the towel. Which is, therefore, no longer holding the towel, quite as well as it should.

choices.label: Turn around immediately
choices.res: "Thank you, my lord," she says, in a very small voice, after the footsteps retreat. She holds the towel with both hands for the rest of the day.

choices.label: Salute back
choices.res: She laughs: a real, startled laugh, the first he's ever heard from her, rough and surprised, like a door that hasn't been opened in years.

choices.label: Stammer helplessly
choices.res: They stand there stammering at each other until a goose interrupts, honking, and the knight loses her last thread of dignity.

image.comp: snapping to attention beside a rain barrel, soaking wet, covering herself with one arm and saluting with the other
image.setting: training yard behind an inn, afternoon

adelheid.title: Knight and Her Lord
adelheid.text: Sam finds Adelheid's secret stash of romance novels in her saddlebag, cracked spines, pressed flowers, a ribbon marking every chapter. Every one is about a knight and her lord. She threatens him with her sword, steel flashing, face scarlet to the roots of her hair. Then asks, very quietly, if he's read the third one.

choices.label: Ask which part of the third one is her favorite
choices.res: She tells him, with the sword still half-drawn and her eyes fixed on a point past his shoulder. It is the chapter in the rain. He takes detailed notes, as is tradition.

choices.label: Hand the books back and promise silence
choices.res: He swears silence on his honor, which causes her to blush deeper. {N} sheathes the sword with great ceremony, and asks if he wants to borrow volume two.

image.comp: pointing a sword at him while clutching a stack of romance novels to her chest, scarlet
image.setting: spartan barracks room

adelheid.title: The Report
adelheid.text: The Order demands Adelheid report on "the sinful nature" of Sam's business. She's been staring at a blank page for three hours, a candle burned to a stub beside her, the quill chewed ragged. Her oath and her honesty are pulling in opposite directions, and the sound of her sword-hilt tapping the desk fills the room.

choices.label: "Tell them the truth."
choices.res: She writes three pages: fair wages, rest days, no one here against her will. She reads them twice and seals them with pride, the wax pressed hard.

choices.label: "Could you... leave some things out?"
choices.res: Her face goes hard. "I will not lie, my lord. Not even for you." It's a long, cold week, and she guards his door like a stranger.

choices.label: Go to the Order with her
choices.res: Sam answers their questions himself, politely, for four hours. Adelheid stands beside him the entire time, shoulders squared, not once looking away.

image.comp: sitting at a desk staring at a blank page, quill frozen, troubled expression
image.setting: barracks room by candlelight

adelheid.title: Swordplay
adelheid.text: Adelheid decides her lord must be able to defend himself, and hands Sam a practice sword in the cold dawn of the training yard. It's much heavier than it looks. Her stance is flawless, her voice crisp: "Feet apart, my lord. Grip firm. Again." Sam's wrists are already complaining, and a rooster is laughing at him.

choices.label: Practice until you drop
choices.res: He drops. Twice. She is quietly, enormously proud, and her hand lingers on his shoulder as she helps him up.

choices.label: Let her win on purpose
choices.res: She knows. She hates that. Her scar-split brow lowers dangerously. "Again, and properly this time."

adelheid.title: The Amended Oath
adelheid.text: Adelheid kneels in the empty chapel hall to renew her oath, the candlelight turning her short hair to silver, then stays kneeling. "My oath was to serve you. I would like to amend it." Her voice is steady but her hand, when she takes his, trembles. "To stand beside you." She rises, and doesn't let go.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: {N} bows her head, stiff with discipline. "I can wait. Don't make it too long." She resumes her post by his door, and stands one pace closer.

marisol.title: Margin Notes
marisol.text: Marisol shows Sam her father's old ledgers in the dusty back room, and her own corrections in the margins: years of tidy, furious red ink, her gold hoops catching the lamp. "He never listened. You actually do." It sounds like an accusation. It isn't. She taps the page with an ink-stained finger and won't look up.

choices.label: Ask her to walk you through one
choices.res: She walks him through a column from six years ago, and he listens to every number. At the end she closes the book gently, as if it had finally been read.

choices.label: Tell her the margins are the best part
choices.res: "The margins are the best part," Sam says. {N} stares at him, then scribbles something in a corner, grinning, and hides it.

image.comp: showing him old ledgers covered in her margin notes, leaning over a desk together
image.setting: owner's office, stacks of ledgers, lamplight

marisol.title: Invoice Ambush
marisol.text: Marisol barges into the washroom mid-argument about invoices, waving a handful of paper, sees Sam in the tub, and keeps arguing. Her gold hoops swing with every point, and her amber eyes fix on the ceiling at the third. She is competitive enough to not give ground even now, and Sam is too wet to take notes.

choices.label: Argue back from the tub
choices.res: He wins, for once. She claims it doesn't count, since he had the unfair advantage of being undressed, and stalks out with her chin high.

choices.label: Ask for some privacy
choices.res: She rolls her eyes, leaves the invoice on the stool, and shuts the door. Firmly. A moment later, through the wood: "Pay it by Friday."

choices.label: Splash her
choices.res: War is declared. The washroom floods, her skirt is soaked, and she retaliates with the sponge. Mira is not amused.

image.comp: standing in a washroom doorway waving an invoice, mid-argument, not leaving
image.setting: steamy wooden washroom, a man in the tub off-frame

marisol.title: House Rules
marisol.text: Marisol beats Sam at cards four times in a row, snapping each hand down with relish, curls bouncing. Then she lets him win once, badly, with a deliberately terrible bluff. "I wanted to see your face," she says, and laughs until she can't breathe, gold hoops swinging, one hand pressed to her ribs.

choices.label: Demand a rematch, with stakes
choices.res: The stakes are a week of ledger duty. He loses again. She lets him pick the penalty, and it takes her a surprisingly long time to say no.

choices.label: Admit that his face was worth it
choices.res: "Worth every coin," Sam says. {N} wipes her eyes and, for once, doesn't reach for a witty retort, only another deck.

image.comp: slapping a winning hand of cards on the table, laughing at his face
image.setting: staff room at night, cards and coins on the table

marisol.title: A Letter
marisol.text: A letter arrives from Marisol's father, creased and salt-stained. He's alive, across the sea, and in debt again. She reads it three times at the ledger desk, jaw tight, and wants to sell something, anything, to bail him out. The ink on her fingers has begun to smear the page.

choices.label: "No. He left you with all of this."
choices.res: "He's not YOUR father." She slams the door, and the hoops on her ears chime. She apologizes the next day; so does he.

choices.label: Send him 300g
choices.res: She stares at the coins for a long time. "You didn't have to." "I know."

cantAfford.res: You can't spare it. She understands. Mostly.

choices.label: Help her write back
choices.res: It takes all night, three drafts and a pot of tea. The letter says no, kindly. She sleeps better than she has in years, her head on the ledger.

image.comp: reading a letter with a stricken expression, his hand on her shoulder
image.setting: owner's office at dusk

marisol.title: Her Mother
marisol.text: Marisol takes Sam to a small grave on the hill above town, wind combing the long grass, a single faded ribbon tied to the stone. Her mother's. She doesn't say much. The gold hoops are still, for once, and her hand is shoved deep in her pocket.

choices.label: Bring flowers
choices.res: She tells him three stories about her mother on the walk back, the lemon cake, the singing, the sums on the backs of invoices. She has never told anyone.

choices.label: Just stand with her
choices.res: After a while she leans against his shoulder, all her competitive edges gone soft, and they watch the clouds cross the stone together.

image.comp: standing at a small grave on a hill with him, holding wildflowers, quiet
image.setting: hilltop graveyard above a fantasy town, overcast

marisol.title: A New Deed
marisol.text: Marisol tears the old deed in half and writes a new one with both their names, her ink-stained fingers steady. The candle gutters in the ledger room where she grew up. "Partners," she says. "In every sense. Don't make me say it twice." Then she kisses him, gold hoops cold against his cheek, and says nothing else for a long while.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: {N} slides the new deed across the desk and taps the line left blank. "I can wait. Don't make it too long." Her pen stays ready.

natsuki.title: Scars and Bets
natsuki.text: Natsuki shows Sam the scar she got her first week here, three years ago, alone, a pale ridge along her ribs just visible above the hem of her tank top. She tells it matter-of-factly, then less so. "I kept thinking: if Sam were here, he'd do something dumb and it'd somehow be fine." She laughs, rough and warm. "Then you showed up and did something dumb."

choices.label: Trace the scar gently with your eyes only
choices.res: He doesn't touch it, but he looks, and he lets her see him looking. She goes quiet in a way she never was in the old neighborhood, and moves the plaster on her cheek back into place.

choices.label: Admit the dumb thing was on purpose
choices.res: "Totally on purpose," Sam lies. {N} grins, rubs her plaster, and punches his shoulder, softer than she'd like to admit.

image.comp: showing him a scar on her arm, sitting on a fence, half-smiling
image.setting: town wall walkway at sunset

natsuki.title: Incoming
natsuki.text: Sam walks into the washroom. Natsuki is in the bath, steam rising, chestnut hair plastered to her forehead, mid-hum. A bar of soap is already in the air at adventurer speed. There's no malice in it, just fifteen years of reflex and a very small, very red face.

choices.label: Duck
choices.res: He doesn't duck fast enough. She feels terrible. She laughs anyway, pressing the heel of her hand against her mouth.

choices.label: Take it like a man
choices.res: Direct hit, right between the eyes. "Nice reflexes, hero," she says, sinking up to her nose in the water, amber eyes bright with mischief.

choices.label: Apologize through the door
choices.res: "Knock next time, idiot!" She sounds like she's grinning, and he hears the soap splash into the tub as she forgives him.

image.comp: throwing a bar of soap at adventurer speed from a bath, furious and blushing
image.setting: steamy wooden washroom

natsuki.title: Almost Taiyaki
natsuki.text: They find a stall selling something almost like taiyaki, warm and sweet-smelling in the evening crowd. Natsuki buys ten. Halfway through the fifth she goes quiet, paper bag crumpling in her fist. "Back home I always figured I'd end up with you someday. Dumb, right?" She doesn't look at him; she watches a lantern bob down the street.

choices.label: Tell her it isn't dumb
choices.res: "It isn't dumb." His voice cracks on the second word. She crushes the bag completely and says nothing, but she doesn't stop him from taking her hand.

choices.label: Steal the last taiyaki to break the tension
choices.res: Sam steals the last one, deadpan. {N} yelps, chases him three stalls down, and laughs herself breathless. Her ears are red when she catches up.

image.comp: eating fish-shaped pastries at a street stall with him, cheeks full, going quiet
image.setting: busy market street, food stalls, afternoon

natsuki.title: Solo Run
natsuki.text: Natsuki took a dangerous dungeon contract without telling anyone. She comes back three days later with a broken arm and a sack of gold, grinning through the grime. The grin falters when she sees his face. Her sword is chipped and her plaster is gone, and she swears the fight was "basically nothing."

choices.label: Yell at her
choices.res: "You don't get to disappear on me twice!" It comes out wrong, too loud, too raw. They don't talk for a while.

choices.label: Patch her up, quietly
choices.res: He doesn't say anything. He doesn't have to. She leans her head against his, breathing out three years of tension.

choices.label: Make her promise
choices.res: "Next time, you come with me," she says, laughing a little. "Deal?" He says deal, and she spits in her palm to shake on it.

image.comp: limping in with a broken arm in a sling and a sack of gold, defiant grin
image.setting: inn entrance hall at night

natsuki.title: Fireworks
natsuki.text: Natsuki bribes an alchemist to make fireworks "like the summer festival back home." They watch from the town wall, legs dangling, a bag of unidentifiable snacks between them. The first burst is the wrong color. The second is almost right, a pink chrysanthemum blooming over Hollowmere's rooftops.

choices.label: Hold her hand
choices.res: Her hand is shaking. Then it isn't. The final burst lights her face gold, and she doesn't take her hand back.

choices.label: Tell her you missed her, all three years
choices.res: She punches his arm. Then she cries. Then she laughs, and the next firework drowns out whatever she says into his shoulder.

image.comp: watching fireworks from the town wall with him, faces lit up
image.setting: town wall at night, colorful fireworks over rooftops

natsuki.title: Door Kicked In
natsuki.text: Natsuki kicks Sam's door open at dawn, red-faced, sword still on her hip, the lock splintering under her boot. Cold morning light spills in behind her. "I spent three years here thinking I'd never see you again. I'm not wasting another day." She kicks the door shut behind her.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: {N} scowls, then softens. "I can wait. Don't make it too long." She repairs the door herself on the way out, badly, and mutters about not being patient.

kanako.title: Sammy
kanako.text: Kanako ruffles Sam's hair and calls him "Sammy" in front of the whole staff. Again. The red lipstick leaves a faint smudge on his cheek, and everyone pretends not to notice. Later she finds him on the back steps, warm lamplight on her beauty mark and the pins coming loose from her hair. "You've grown up a lot, haven't you? When did that happen?"

choices.label: Tell her it happened somewhere around the truck
choices.res: "Somewhere around the truck," he says. She laughs, loud and bright, then goes quiet and watches him a beat too long over the rim of her glass.

choices.label: Let her ruffle your hair again
choices.res: He bows his head and lets her. {N}'s fingers linger in his hair a second past the joke, and then she tucks a loose pin back into place and says nothing.

image.comp: ruffling his hair in front of the staff, laughing
image.setting: lively bar during staff meeting

kanako.title: Shampoo
kanako.text: Kanako walks in on Sam in the bath, doesn't blink, sets the shampoo on the edge of the tub, and keeps chatting about the bar schedule, like it's nothing. Her red lipstick and the beauty mark under her eye are the only things steady in the steam. Sam's ears, meanwhile, are doing something unprecedented.

choices.label: Insist she leave
choices.res: "So shy!" she giggles, and goes. Her laugh carries all the way down the corridor, a touch too bright, and she forgets the schedule on the stool.

choices.label: Act just as casual
choices.res: She falters. Just a little. Her eyes flick down, then away, and the lipstick-red smile stays fixed. Interesting.

choices.label: "I'm a grown man, Kanako."
choices.res: She stops mid-sentence. Looks at him. Leaves without a word, and he can hear her not laughing all the way down the hall.

image.comp: setting a shampoo bottle on the edge of a tub, chatting casually, not blinking
image.setting: steamy wooden washroom, a man in the tub off-frame

kanako.title: Since When
kanako.text: A drunk client gets grabby with Kanako and Sam steps in without thinking, a hand on the man's wrist, a voice he didn't know he had. Afterward the bar is quiet, glasses ringing faintly. She leans on the counter, silent for a long time. "Since when do you protect me?" She doesn't ruffle his hair. She just looks at him, like she's seeing him for the first time.

choices.label: Tell her since always
choices.res: "Since always," he says, and it comes out smaller than he intended. She takes a slow breath. When she nods, her hand rests on his for a moment.

choices.label: Pour her a drink and say nothing
choices.res: He pours her a glass without a word. {N} drinks it slowly, looking at him over the rim, and for once she's the one who forgets to joke.

image.comp: standing behind him after he's stepped in front of a drunk client, surprised soft expression
image.setting: busy bar at night

kanako.title: Matchmaker
kanako.text: Kanako has found Sam "a nice girl" and set up a dinner, a candle on the table and her own best lipstick on, fussing at his collar. She's very proud of herself. Her laugh is the loudest thing in the room. Her fingers, straightening his cuff, are not quite steady.

choices.label: Go on the date to make her happy
choices.res: She asks how it went. Twice. She doesn't seem happy with either answer, and she wipes the same glass for a quarter of an hour.

choices.label: "It's always been you. You know that."
choices.res: Kanako opens her mouth, closes it, and leaves. She doesn't sleep that night. Neither does he.

choices.label: Politely refuse
choices.res: "You're impossible," she sighs, and fusses with his collar once more. She looks relieved, and a little guilty about it.

image.comp: proudly presenting a nervous young woman at a dinner table to him, beaming matchmaker grin
image.setting: small restaurant, candles

kanako.title: Last Call
kanako.text: Kanako finds a bar that's almost like a snack bar back home, with a low counter, a cracked mirror and a smoky amber light, and takes Sam there, just the two of them. There's a lute, and a very drunk bard willing to lend it. She orders for both of them, the way she did for six years across the hallway.

choices.label: Sing, badly
choices.res: She joins in. They are both terrible, the bard weeps with laughter, and it's the best night either of them has had in this world.

choices.label: Ask her to sing
choices.res: Her voice is soft, a little rough from years of smoke and laughter. She sings the whole song looking at him.

image.comp: singing karaoke with a lute-playing bard in a tiny bar, the man laughing beside her
image.setting: tiny cozy bar like a snack bar, warm lights

kanako.title: Not the Boy Next Door
kanako.text: Kanako corners Sam in the kitchen late at night, the lamp low, a pot cooling on the stove, flustered for once in her life, red lipstick smudged where she's been biting her lip. "I spent six years telling myself you were the boy next door. You're not. You haven't been for a long time." She kisses him, laughs at her own blush, and kisses him again.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: {N} laughs, but it's soft. "I can wait. Don't make it too long." She ruffles his hair, slowly this time, like a question.

akari.title: The Umbrella
akari.text: Akari finds Sam on a bench in the afternoon crush of the market street, an umbrella folded in her lap that the cloudless sky has no use for. She admits she'd been a few steps behind him and Kenta at the crosswalk that day, the umbrella she didn't need shoved in her bag and a bag of his favorite candy crinkling in her pocket. "Just walking by," she says, too quickly, picking at the umbrella's strap. Then, in a smaller voice: "Kenta stopped to tie his shoe. He's fine. He's definitely fine." Her smile is very bright, and her eyes are not. She looks at Sam as if daring him to disagree.

choices.label: "He's fine. He's the luckiest guy I know."
choices.res: Something in her shoulders unlocks. She leans against his arm and, for a whole minute, the loudest girl in the market does not make a single joke, which is a personal record. "Thanks for not saying it was nothing," she mumbles.

choices.label: Keep it light, just nod along
choices.res: "Yeah," she says, relieved and a little disappointed, and snaps the umbrella open under the clear sky just to have something to do. "Obviously. Totally fine."

image.comp: sitting beside him holding a folded umbrella in her lap, a brave bright smile with worried eyes
image.setting: busy market street, late afternoon

akari.title: What a Coincidence
akari.text: Steam rolls out when Sam pushes open the washroom door, and there is Akari in the tub with her chin propped on her folded arms, bubbles piled artfully around her, a single rubber duck positioned like a prop. It is obvious she has been waiting a good while; her fingertips are wrinkled. She gasps, one hand fluttering to her mouth, a performance worthy of a very bad play. "Oh no. Sam. You've caught me. What a coincidence." The duck bobs between them, unconvinced.

choices.label: Back out and close the door
choices.res: "Coward!" she yells after him, over the sound of a furious duck-squeak. The door shuts on her cackling, and he can hear her sulking happily for a full minute afterward.

choices.label: "You're Kenta's sister."
choices.res: A sponge hits the door as it closes. "I KNOW whose sister I am!" A minute later, from inside, much quieter, the water barely stirring: "...I'm tired of only being that."

choices.label: Burst out laughing
choices.res: She tries to stay offended, lips pressed flat, eyebrows drawn down. It lasts four seconds before she slides under the bubbles and laughs until the water sloshes onto the floor.

image.comp: lounging in a bath, obviously waiting, fake-gasping with a hand over her mouth
image.setting: steamy wooden washroom

akari.title: Game Night
akari.text: Akari organizes a staff "game night" in the lounge, with a card game she half remembers from Kenta's apartment and invents the rest of as she goes, rules shouted over the clinking of mugs. She wins. Loudly, with a victory dance. Halfway through the next round she realizes Sam has been quietly sliding her the right cards for an hour, a nudge here, a pointed pause there, and the whole table goes slightly blurry for her as she stops mid-cheer. "You always did that," she says, very quiet in the lamplight. "I thought I was imagining it."

choices.label: Stay with her after the others drift off
choices.res: When the others have gone she gathers the cards into a clumsy stack and bumps her shoulder against his. "Teach me to cheat properly," she says, "and I'll let you win once." The lamp burns lower, and neither of them reaches to turn it up.

choices.label: Keep the mood light and deal another hand
choices.res: "Rematch," she announces, and shuffles so badly that cards spray the floor. She laughs it off, but her eyes linger on him a second longer than the joke needs.

image.comp: holding a hand of cards up to her face, peeking over them at him with a stunned, delighted grin
image.setting: inn lounge, staff gathered around a table, lamplight

akari.title: Useless
akari.text: A client complains about Akari, loudly, in front of half the common room, about her fumbled pouring and her chatter. Later Sam hears a sniffle behind the linen closet door and finds her sitting on a stack of folded sheets, a towel clutched to her chest, mascara smudged. "I'm useless," she says. "I'm just the person who tagged along behind you and Kenta, carrying the snacks." She wipes her eyes with the towel. "I wanted to be someone you'd notice."

choices.label: "You don't have to do this. You can quit."
choices.res: "That's not what I wanted you to say." She doesn't come out of the closet for an hour, and the linens are folded with fierce, furious precision when she finally does.

choices.label: Train her yourself, every evening
choices.res: Every evening for a week, after close, he walks her through it, patient and bad at demonstrating. She is clumsy for three days and then, abruptly, not. She gets better. She gets a lot better, and by the end she's showing off.

choices.label: Tell her about your own failures
choices.res: He tells her about the truck, about the three jobs he failed to keep, about the time he cried in a convenience store over a vending machine. By the end she is laughing through her tears and hitting him with a towel.

image.comp: crying in a linen closet hugging a stack of towels
image.setting: cramped linen closet, a sliver of light

akari.title: Drama Date
akari.text: Akari demands a "proper date, like in the dramas": umbrella in the rain, a dramatic run toward the station (there is no station), a long meaningful look under a streetlamp. She has storyboarded it. The rain obliges, which she finds suspicious. Halfway through she drops the act, umbrella wilting in her fist and her hair plastered to her cheek. "I've rehearsed this in my head for years," she admits. "I'm terrible at the real thing."

choices.label: Commit to every drama cliche
choices.res: He tilts the umbrella, gazes meaningfully, and at the end trips into her arms, on purpose, with an actor's gasp. She nearly dies of happiness, and then of laughing.

choices.label: Do it your own way
choices.res: A walk in the drizzle, warm buns from the bakery, a quiet bench under the eaves where they share the last one. "...Okay," she admits, leaning on him. "This is better than the dramas."

image.comp: running dramatically through the rain toward him holding an umbrella
image.setting: lantern-lit street in the rain

akari.title: Not Kenta's Sister
akari.text: Akari climbs the ladder onto the roof where Sam is hiding from the paperwork, a lantern in one hand, her hair whipped loose by the evening wind. She sits down across from him, then stands again, too restless. "I've had a crush on you for years, and I'm done keeping it to myself. I'm not Kenta's sister up here. I'm a grown woman and I know what I want. It's you." Her voice cracks on the last word, but she doesn't look away. This time, Sam doesn't climb down.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Akari nods, brave and bright and just a little crushed. "I can wait," she says, tapping the lantern. "Don't make me wait longer than a drama season, okay?"

lara.title: The Step Below
lara.text: Lara finds Sam on the back steps after close, a lantern guttering beside him, and sits one step below, knees together, hands folded in her lap like a child waiting outside an office. In a low, careful voice she tells him how she tracked rumors of a stranger in a grey hoodie across three provinces, sleeping in stables and chapels, her black coat getting shabbier with every road. "I couldn't stay anywhere you weren't," she says. "I know that's not healthy. I know." She is looking at his boots, not his face, and her dark lipstick is chewed at the corner.

choices.label: "I'm really glad you found me."
choices.res: She lets out a long, shaky breath, as if she's been holding it since Alder Street. A moth circles the lantern, and she watches it instead of crying, which for Lara is the same thing.

choices.label: "You're allowed a life of your own, Lara."
choices.res: She nods slowly, as though it's a lesson she'll need to learn more than once. She doesn't leave, but she looks out at the dark street instead of at him, and he can almost hear her turning the idea over, one careful page at a time.

image.comp: sitting one step below him on a back staircase at night, hands folded in her lap, looking up at him with dark kohl-lined eyes
image.setting: back steps of a lantern-lit inn at night

lara.title: Can't Sleep
lara.text: At midnight Lara carries fresh towels to the washroom because she couldn't sleep, and walks in on Sam in the tub. She freezes in the doorway, arms full of linen, the stack held up to hide everything above her nose, lace cuffs trembling. Steam curls around her black dress. "I'm so sorry. I'm so sorry. I'm just going to... stand here." She does not move. A drip falls from the tap, loud as a clock in the silence, and the towels creep a little higher.

choices.label: Laugh and ask her to leave the towels
choices.res: She sets them down with enormous, ceremonial care and retreats, and he hears her laughing, once, short and surprised, in the empty hall.

choices.label: "Stay and talk, if you can't sleep."
choices.res: She sits on the edge of the tub with her back turned and tells him about the night noises of the orphanage, the pipes, the coughing, the matron's keys. By the end she's leaning against the wood, nearly asleep, her voice gone soft and slow.

choices.label: Send her to bed
choices.res: "Of course." She goes at once, silent as a cat. In the morning she apologizes four times, and the fourth is to the towel rack.

image.comp: frozen in a washroom doorway, arms full of folded towels hiding most of her face, mortified
image.setting: steamy wooden washroom at night

lara.title: A Lamp in the Window
lara.text: Whenever Sam is out, Lara leaves a lamp lit in the courtyard window. Tonight he's out very late, and a cold fog has settled over Hollowmere. When he returns she is sitting under that lamp in her black shawl, a book open on her knee and not a single page turned, moths drifting around the glass. She stands, then doesn't know what to do with her hands. "I wasn't waiting," she says. "I was keeping it warm."

choices.label: Sit with her
choices.res: They share the bench and the shawl, which smells of lavender and old paper. She leans against his shoulder and, for once, doesn't ask whether he's tired of her.

choices.label: "Come out with me next time."
choices.res: She says "maybe," very softly, and tugs the shawl closer. It is better than the "no" she'd have given last month, and they both know it.

image.comp: sitting under a courtyard lamp in a black shawl with a book, looking up as he returns
image.setting: lantern-lit courtyard at night, moths around the light

lara.title: Don't Go
lara.text: The house needs Sam in the capital for three days to settle a supplier dispute. Lara hears it in the corridor, a stack of folded sheets in her arms, and goes white as the linen. She follows him to his room and grips the doorframe so hard her knuckles blanch. "Everyone who says they'll come back... I know how this goes, Sam. I know." Her eyes are enormous and perfectly dry. She doesn't cry. That is worse.

choices.label: "I'll never leave you."
choices.res: It's what she wants to hear. It isn't quite true, and both of them know it. She nods, holds on a little too tightly when he hugs her, and the three days are very long.

choices.label: "I can't promise forever. I promise I'll come back."
choices.res: She cries, but it's a different kind, the kind that loosens something. She presses her room key into his palm, warm from her fist. "So you have to return it," she whispers.

choices.label: Hand her the linen schedule to run while you're gone
choices.res: She runs the house for three days with ledgers and lists and not a single crooked pillow. When he returns, she meets him at the door, proud in a way that has nothing to do with him, and that is exactly the point.

image.comp: gripping a doorframe with both hands, pale, dark eyes wide, ponytail swinging
image.setting: dim inn corridor at night

lara.title: Midnight Garden
lara.text: Lara invites Sam to the courtyard at midnight, as though she'd thought hard about it and decided to ask first. Under the moon, in a corner no one else bothered with, she has planted a patch of white flowers that glow faintly, like spilled milk-light. She shows him the little paths of pebbles she laid, the watering can with her initials scratched in. She says it's hers, and that she'd like him to see it. "I made something," she says. "Even if you weren't here."

choices.label: Tell her it's beautiful, and mean it
choices.res: She laughs, shaky and surprised, and tucks a glowing blossom behind his ear. "Now you're in the garden too," she says, and doesn't look away this time.

choices.label: Plant the next row together
choices.res: She teaches him to space the seeds with two fingers' width between them. He does it wrong, over and over. She lets him, because it's his row now, and kneels beside it in the dirt in her good black dress.

image.comp: kneeling in a patch of glowing white night flowers, offering a small blossom up to him, shy smile
image.setting: moonlit courtyard garden of pale night-blooming flowers

lara.title: Being Left
lara.text: On the roof, under a clear sky, Lara stands with her hands wrapped in her shawl and says it slowly, each word chosen. "I used to think loving someone meant never being left. I think it's closer to... being able to be left, and still be me." Her voice steadies as she goes. "I want you because I choose you. Not because I'm afraid." She kisses him, and for the first time in her life she is the one who leads him inside, and the door closes behind them.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Lara nods, and this time it doesn't look like a door closing. "I can wait," she says, steady. "I'll keep the lamp lit. Don't make it too long."

emily.title: Username
emily.text: Emily asks Sam to meet her on the bridge over the canal after close. She has clearly rehearsed this, and has also clearly forgotten every word, twisting the strap of her satchel as lamplight shivers on the water below. "Okay. So. This is going to sound insane," she says, and then she says his old forum username out loud, in a world where nobody should know it. Her wolf ears are flat against her hair, and her tail is wrapped around her own leg. "Please tell me I didn't just say a random string of letters to a stranger."

choices.label: Say "Shadowkin?"
choices.res: She makes a noise he has only ever seen typed as a keysmash. Then she grabs his sleeve with both hands and holds on, tail thumping the bridge stones, until the lamp oil needs a refill.

choices.label: "You still owe me the end of that campaign."
choices.res: "It was YOUR turn to post!" she says, outraged, ears snapping upright, and then she starts crying and laughing at the same time and has to take off her glasses to wipe them.

image.comp: standing on a canal bridge at night, hands clasped, wolf ears flat, glasses, hopeful and terrified smile
image.setting: stone bridge over a canal, lamplight on the water

emily.title: Bath Lag
emily.text: Sam opens the washroom door and finds Emily in the tub, a notebook balanced on the rim, glasses fogged, one damp wolf ear flopped sideways as she mutters in what is unmistakably her old character's gravelly narrator voice. "And then the wolf drew her blade and said..." She looks up. Her tail slaps the water, soaking the notebook's edge. "I was drafting dialogue," she says, mortified. "Out loud. Like a normal person."

choices.label: Apologize and back out
choices.res: "It's fine!" she squeaks. That evening a note slides under his door: brb dying of embarrassment, signed with a tiny wolf doodle chewing its own tail.

choices.label: Answer in your old character's voice
choices.res: She stares, then answers back in character, and they finish the whole scene through the door with Sam politely facing the hallway. She laughs so hard the water sloshes, and the narrator voice cracks completely.

choices.label: Stand there, flustered
choices.res: Her ears go straight back. "Lag," she whispers, clutching the notebook. "You're lagging. Please reconnect." He tries, fails, and she giggles into her hands until her glasses fall in the water.

image.comp: in a tub with a notebook on the rim, fogged glasses, wolf ears perked up in surprise, tail splashing
image.setting: steamy wooden washroom

emily.title: Session Zero
emily.text: Emily talks Sam into running a campaign again, on paper, in the lounge after close. She has carved dice faces into wooden cubes and written character sheets for both of them in tidy forum-style headers, her tail sweeping the rug as she sets out snacks. It's the same story they abandoned years ago, picked up mid-scene. The fire pops. Halfway through the session, her character says something to his that isn't in any of the old logs.

choices.label: Answer in character
choices.res: He does. She drops a die, picks it up, drops it again, and finally hides behind her character sheet with only the tips of her ears showing, quivering.

choices.label: Ask, out of character, if she meant it
choices.res: "OOC?" she says, very small, ears dipping behind the paper. "...Yeah. OOC, I meant it." The dice sit forgotten between them.

image.comp: sitting cross-legged on a sofa with hand-drawn character sheets and wooden dice, peeking over a sheet with a shy smile, tail swishing
image.setting: cozy lounge after close, fireplace glow

emily.title: Last Seen
emily.text: Emily shows Sam a page of her notebook where she copied out, from memory, the last thing she ever sent him on the forum: "you there?" It was never answered. The pencil marks are smudged where her thumb has rubbed them for months. "I kept checking for three weeks," she says quietly, ears drooped. "Then I woke up here. Sometimes I think if I fall asleep wrong, I'll wake up back in my dorm and you'll still be 'last seen' forever."

choices.label: "I'm here."
choices.res: She reads his face like a chat window, waiting for the typing indicator. Then she nods, and holds his sleeve for a long time anyway, just to be sure it's real.

choices.label: Write the reply under it
choices.res: He takes her pencil and writes under her line: yeah. sorry for the lag. She presses the notebook to her chest, her tail thumping once, and laughs wetly into the cover.

choices.label: "Let's not think about it."
choices.res: "Right. Sure." Her ears droop and her tail goes still. She spends the evening rereading her notebook alone by the fire, and the page stays dry only by effort.

image.comp: holding an open notebook toward him, ears drooped, tail low, glasses, fear in her eyes
image.setting: lamp-lit lounge corner at night

emily.title: New Constellations
emily.text: Under a full moon Emily takes Sam up onto the roof with a blanket and her notebook. None of the stars match the ones back home, so she has been naming the constellations after their old campaign: the Cursed Lute, the Bard Who Never Posted, the Wolf and the Idiot. She lets her ears and tail relax, finally, at ease in the silver light. "I figured," she says, "if we're stuck here, we should at least have our own sky."

choices.label: Name one together
choices.res: They argue happily for an hour over a single cluster of stars and settle on The Streak. She writes it down in her best forum-header lettering, tail wagging the blanket into a heap.

choices.label: Ask which one is her
choices.res: She points to two stars close together and doesn't explain. She tucks her ears under his chin for a moment, and she doesn't have to.

image.comp: lying on a blanket on a rooftop in moonlight pointing at the stars, notebook open, wolf ears relaxed, glancing at him with soft eyes
image.setting: slate rooftop under a full moon, a lantern beside her

emily.title: More Than a Username
emily.text: Emily stops in the doorway of Sam's room, notebook hugged to her chest, tail wrapped around her own ankle. "For six years you were a username," she says. "My favorite one. I never wanted more than that, and then I got a whole person, and it turns out I do." She is trembling, ears flat. "I'm bad at saying things out loud. So, short version." She takes his hand, and her grip is much surer than her voice. "Stay online." The door closes behind them.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Emily nods, ears wobbling. "I can wait," she says, clutching the notebook. "Just don't go idle on me."

lirael.title: Whoever Finds This
lirael.text: Lirael meets Sam at the old iron postbox in the alley after close, a single lamp throwing their shadows long across the cobbles. From her satchel she draws a yellowed letter, soft at the folds from years of handling: the very first one, addressed to "Whoever finds this." She reads it aloud in a clear, careful clerk's voice that trembles at the end. "I never thought anyone would write back." Her long ears are drooping, and her fingers smooth the paper as if it might tear. "And then you did."

choices.label: "Thank you for writing first."
choices.res: Her satchel strap slips from her fingers and clinks against the cobbles, loud in the quiet alley. She covers her face with the letter, ears trembling, and does not seem to mind that he can see.

choices.label: Take the letter and read your own reply
choices.res: He reads it aloud from memory, and she mouths the words along with him; she has known them by heart for years. When he stumbles over a line she supplies it, softly, without looking.

image.comp: holding a yellowed letter against her chest beside an old iron postbox, long ears drooping, shy and tearful smile
image.setting: lamp-lit alley beside an old iron postbox at night

lirael.title: Ink Stains
lirael.text: Sam opens the washroom door and finds Lirael in the tub, a stack of waterproofed letters balanced on the rim, reading with a soft smile and a damp pencil behind one long ear. She looks up. Her hand slaps the water and a fan of drops lands across the top page. "I read them here," she says, mortified, pressing the letters to her chest. "It's the only quiet room in the building."

choices.label: Apologize and back out
choices.res: "It's fine!" she squeaks. That evening a note appears under his door, three neat lines in her sorter's hand, signed with a tiny drawn quill that has blotted a little at the tip.

choices.label: "Which one are you on?"
choices.res: She holds up the letter. He reads it from the doorway, politely addressing the ceiling. She laughs so hard the water sloshes, and the ink on the rim runs in a pretty blue stream.

choices.label: Stand there, flustered
choices.res: The tips of her ears go pink. "Please say something," she whispers. He tries, fails, and she giggles into her hands, a rare, bubbling sound that echoes off the wooden walls.

image.comp: reading a letter in a tub with a stack of letters on the rim, long ears perked up in surprise, hand splashing the water
image.setting: steamy wooden washroom

lirael.title: Notes Across the Sofa
lirael.text: They fall into an easy habit: sitting at opposite ends of the lounge sofa after close, writing each other notes instead of talking, and passing them across with their feet. It is a ridiculous, wonderful way to flirt. The fire ticks, paper rustles, and Lirael's replies grow longer every night, her handwriting looping as she gets braver. Tonight's note has a P.S. in very small letters, crowded into the corner like a secret.

choices.label: Stay with her
choices.res: He reads the P.S. aloud, and she buries her face in a cushion, ears trembling, then scribbles a reply and kicks it across the sofa before she can think better of it.

choices.label: Write one back about how you feel
choices.res: She reads it three times, mouthing the words, then folds it into precise thirds and tucks it into her satchel, beside the others, where he can see how many there are.

image.comp: curled at one end of a sofa writing a note on her knee, one foot swinging, peeking over the paper with a shy smile
image.setting: cozy inn lounge, fireplace glow

lirael.title: Wrong Address
lirael.text: A letter arrives for Sam with no stamp, no postmark, and an address in a handwriting he hasn't used in years: his own, from long ago. It reads: "To whoever I become. I hope you're not lonely anymore." Lirael reads over his shoulder, and the sorting-room hum around them seems to fade. She goes very still, long ears flat. "If a letter can cross," she says quietly, "so can a person. What if the box takes you back?"

choices.label: "I'm not going anywhere."
choices.res: She nods, and holds his sleeve for a long time anyway, thumb worrying the cuff, as though it were a letter she might lose in the post.

choices.label: Write a reply together
choices.res: They write two words and post them: Not lonely. The old box hums under her palm, a low warm note. She is still smiling when it falls silent.

choices.label: Burn the letter
choices.res: "You can't burn what's already happened," she says. She spends the night sweeping the postbox in silence, one slow stroke after another, ears low.

image.comp: reading a letter over his shoulder, ears drooped, fear in her eyes
image.setting: lamp-lit lounge corner at night

lirael.title: Full Moon Post
lirael.text: Under a full moon Lirael takes Sam up onto the post house roof to sort the night's collection by lantern light, bundles tied with twine, the slate cold beneath them. She lets her shoulders and ears relax, her clerk's stiffness softening in the silver air. Between letters, she hums the tune she once wrote in the margin of her second note, and he realizes he's been humming it for years without knowing where it came from.

choices.label: Hum along
choices.res: She stops sorting and just listens, ears tilted toward him, and then joins the harmony in a thin sweet voice. The letters lie forgotten in her lap.

choices.label: Help her sort the last bag
choices.res: He puts every letter in the wrong slot. She re-sorts every one, grinning, and says it's the best mistake she's ever seen, and keeps the worst-sorted one to herself.

image.comp: sitting on a post house roof in moonlight sorting letters, long ears relaxed, humming, glancing at him with soft eyes
image.setting: slate rooftop under a full moon, a lantern beside her

lirael.title: Meeting the Man
lirael.text: Lirael sets her satchel down in the doorway of Sam's room, a thing she has never done in front of him. "For ten years I wrote to a name," she says. "I'd like to meet the man." She is trembling, ears dipping, one foot hooked around her own ankle. "I'm not good at saying things out loud. So I'll say the short version." She takes his hand, and her ink-stained fingertips are warm. "Stay." The door closes behind them.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Lirael nods and straightens her satchel strap, gracious as a clerk with a delayed parcel. "I can wait," she says. "I've waited longer for less. Just do write back."

ella.title: Dinner Is a Competition
ella.text: Ella challenges Sam to dinner as a competition: whoever orders the better meal wins. She arrives early, naturally, and has already studied the menu. Over the second course she puts down her fork, and the candle flame steadies between them. "I was across the street. I saw the truck. For three years I've told myself I'd never speak of it." Her hand is steady on the glass, but her knuckles are white. "I'm speaking of it now. Because you're here. Because I can."

choices.label: Reach across the table
choices.res: She lets him hold her hand and does not comment, though her pulse beats against his thumb. Then, quietly, a ghost of her usual crispness: "That counts as a point to you."

choices.label: Order dessert and change the subject gently
choices.res: She follows the pivot like a professional, blinking once, composure settled. "The tart. Obviously." Under the table, her foot finds his and stays there.

image.comp: sitting across a candlelit dinner table from him, fork set down, serious and vulnerable, hand on her wine glass
image.setting: private corner table in a lantern-lit restaurant

ella.title: Scoring Points
ella.text: Sam opens the washroom door and finds Ella in the tub, hair pinned up with a pencil, a thick book propped on the soap dish, a glasses-fogged glare aimed squarely at the intruder. Steam curls around her. "You didn't knock," she says. "That's a point to me." She doesn't cover up, since the moral high ground is more valuable than modesty, and she turns a page with deliberate calm.

choices.label: Concede the point and leave
choices.res: "Good." She tallies it in the margin of the book with a pencil. Later she leaves a cup of tea outside his door, which she scores as a draw.

choices.label: "Then I'll earn it back."
choices.res: "Oh?" The corner of her mouth moves. "Name your terms." They negotiate through the steam for far longer than the situation warrants, and neither of them seems to want to finish.

else.res: "Out," she says, with great dignity, and points the pencil at the door. "The point stands. Also, you're letting the heat out."

choices.label: Compliment her and mean it
choices.res: She goes very still, and a delicate pink climbs up her throat to her ears. "That... wasn't in my scoring system," she says, and for once she doesn't have a rebuttal.

image.comp: in a bath, hair pinned up, a book propped beside her, fixing the doorway with a cool unimpressed glare
image.setting: steamy wooden washroom

ella.title: The Leaderboard
ella.text: Ella turns the staff's daily chores into a points tournament, with a chalkboard leaderboard, little prizes and an appeals process with a very strict deadline. Morale in the house triples; even the cook has started saluting her. She has also, without telling anyone, assigned Sam a score of her own: a secret column in her notebook headed Observations. She is only caught when it falls out of her apron into the flour dust, and lies there, wide open.

choices.label: Stay with her
choices.res: He reads it aloud, politely, because she has frozen. The column contains seventeen entries, several about his handwriting. She says nothing at all and doesn't leave.

choices.label: Hand it back unread
choices.res: She takes it with great dignity and tucks it away. "You are," she says, crisply, "unbelievably annoying." It sounds, for once, like a compliment.

image.comp: holding a leaderboard chalkboard, caught as a small notebook falls out of her apron, mortified and composed at once
image.setting: busy inn kitchen with staff cheering in the background

ella.title: The Offer
ella.text: A merchant house in the capital offers Ella a post as chief of accounts: a salary, a title, a corner office with her name lettered on the door. It's everything she has ever wanted, on paper. She lays the letter in front of Sam in the quiet ledger room without a word, hands flat on the desk, and watches his face with the intensity of someone grading an exam she has already written the answers to.

choices.label: "Take it. You'd be the best they've ever had."
choices.res: She nods once. "I hate how much I wanted you to say that," she mutters, smoothing the letter. She doesn't answer the merchants for a week.

choices.label: "Stay. Beat me here."
choices.res: "That's cheating," she says, eyes bright. She turns the letter down the next morning, in writing, with a flourish of the pen that nearly tears the page.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.res: She folds the letter, tucks it away, and gives him a mark he can't read. The house is colder for days, and the leaderboard stays unchalked.

image.comp: sitting at a desk with a sealed offer letter in front of her, watching him with a level searching gaze
image.setting: ledger room, lamplight, neat stacks of paper

ella.title: Rematch
ella.text: Ella sets up a chessboard in the courtyard at dusk, with rules, a brass clock and a hand-lettered scoreboard that reads SAM vs. ELLA - GAME 1 OF 1. They play for two hours without speaking, the lanterns coming on one by one, the clock ticking. At the end, she has him cornered. She looks at the board. She looks at him. She doesn't make the winning move.

choices.label: Offer a draw
choices.res: "Accepted," she says, much too quickly, and tips her king over herself. "As a purely tactical choice."

choices.label: Tell her to take the win
choices.res: She takes it, and cheers, genuinely, a bright unguarded whoop, and then buys him dinner out of sheer guilt, and pays for the good wine.

image.comp: leaning over a chessboard, one hand hovering above a piece, looking up at him instead of the game
image.setting: lantern-lit courtyard table at dusk, chessboard between them

ella.title: First Place
ella.text: Ella stops him on the stairs, a pencil in her hair and a ledger under her arm, her chin lifted for a fight. "I have been second to you for years, and I have never minded. Don't tell anyone." She takes the pencil out of her hair, lets it fall down around her shoulders, and meets his eyes. "I'm not competing anymore. I'd like to be on your side of the board." She kisses him, decisively, as if it were the winning move.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Ella nods briskly, as if filing it. "I can wait," she says. "But I'm tracking the delay, Sam. Don't make it too long."

ione.title: Three Questions
ione.text: Ione brings Sam tea on the back steps, exactly how he takes it, at exactly the temperature he likes. "I will answer any question you ask," she says, "except three. I won't tell you where I came from, how I came, or how the story ends." She sits with perfect posture and a faint hum, silver-white hair silvered further by the dusk. "The rest is yours." Sam, flailing, asks her what she likes. She is quiet for so long he thinks she's frozen. "Nobody has asked me that before," she says.

choices.label: "Then tell me what you like."
choices.res: She lists seven things, slowly: rain, the smell of tea, the hum of a crowded room, and, last, quietly, "you." Her status light glows gold, and she looks faintly astonished at it.

choices.label: Let her keep her secrets
choices.res: She tilts her head. "That is the kindest answer I could have received." Her shoulders lower by one precise degree, and her hum drops to something almost like a sigh.

image.comp: sitting upright on a back step holding a teacup, silver-white hair and a softly glowing temple light, looking at him with calm curiosity
image.setting: back steps of a lantern-lit inn at dusk

ione.title: Warm Water
ione.text: Ione has discovered the bath. Sam walks in to find her seated in the water, perfectly still, eyes closed, silver hair floating and her status light glowing a fascinated gold. "I have read about this for years," she says, not opening her eyes. "No document prepared me for the temperature." Steam beads on her lashes. She makes no attempt to cover up, since it hasn't occurred to her to.

choices.label: Sit on the edge and tell her about baths
