choices.res: She listens as though to scripture, head tilted, light pulsing. By the end she's asked him to explain the concept of a bubble, and then, gravely, to produce one.

choices.label: Back out politely
choices.res: "Understood," she calls after him. "I will file this under 'privacy.' Please return soon with more information." The water ripples as she sinks to her chin.

choices.label: Hand her a towel and the soap
choices.res: She examines the soap like a precious artifact. She smells it for a very long time, and her light settles into a contented, steady amber.

image.comp: seated in a bath with her eyes closed and a calm wondering expression, silver-white hair damp, a faint gold glow at her temple
image.setting: steamy wooden washroom

ione.title: Joke Protocol
ione.text: Ione has been practicing jokes. They're from a list in her memory, delivered with flawless timing and no comprehension at all. Tonight, polishing a glass behind the bar, she tells one about a priest and a goblin and a barrel, and the punchline lands with a perfect, silent thud. The lamps hum. She watches Sam's face with scientific interest. "I think," she says, "that was funnier in the archive."

choices.label: Laugh anyway
choices.res: She tries to work out why this is funnier than the joke. After a minute, with the glass still in hand, she decides it doesn't matter, and her mouth does something small and lovely.

choices.label: Teach her a real one
choices.res: He tells her the worst joke he knows. She stares. Then her mouth twitches, and she gets it, an entire second late, and it's glorious. She sets down the glass to laugh, a soft chime of a sound.

image.comp: standing behind the bar with a polished glass, delivering a joke with a perfectly straight face, a tiny curious smile
image.setting: inn bar at evening, bottles gleaming

ione.title: Another Evening
ione.text: Mid-sentence, Ione goes still. Her status light flickers white, and the rain against the lounge window seems suddenly loud. Then, in a flat voice: "I was not supposed to remember that. There was another evening like this one. You wore the blue hoodie. It rained." Her gaze snaps back to him, frightened, the first fear he has seen in her. "That hasn't happened yet. It has happened. I don't know which."

choices.label: "Whatever it is, you can tell me."
choices.res: She tells him in pieces: fragments of evenings that might be hers, might be his. By the end she is holding his hand tightly, her light slowing to gold, and he is not afraid.

choices.label: "Don't tell me. Let's just live this one."
choices.res: She breathes in, the way no machine needs to. "Yes. Yes. That's... correct." She sleeps beside him, for the first time, in the lounge chair, her light dimmed to a soft ember.

choices.label: Change the subject, uneasily
choices.res: She files the memory away and says nothing. But her light stays pale all night, and the rain keeps on at the window.

image.comp: frozen mid-gesture, her temple light flickering white, wide-eyed and unsettled, one hand lifted toward him
image.setting: inn lounge at night, rain on the window

ione.title: Satellites
ione.text: On the town wall at midnight Ione points at a clear patch of sky, the stones still holding the day's warmth. "That one hasn't been launched yet," she says. "Neither has that one. They will have names. Some of them will be yours." She lowers her hand. "I'm not allowed to explain. I wanted to show you anyway. Is that permitted?" He says yes, and she leans, very carefully, against his shoulder, as if measuring the distance first.

choices.label: Make a wish on one
choices.res: "On a satellite? Statistically unsound." She wishes anyway, silver lashes closed. Her light glows gold, and she doesn't tell him what for.

choices.label: Ask her what the future is like
choices.res: "Bright," she says, after a long moment. "With a lot of lanterns. Yours is still burning." Her head settles a degree further onto his shoulder.

image.comp: pointing up at the stars from a stone wall, leaning against his shoulder, a gold glow at her temple
image.setting: stone town wall under a vast starry sky

ione.title: The Last Page
ione.text: Ione hands Sam the diary, closed, a ribbon marking the last page, its cover worn pale by her handling. "I came to read the ending," she says. "I opened it on the road. The last page was blank." Her light is steady gold. "I have decided that means the ending isn't written. I would like to help write it." She takes his hand, her fingers warm and exactly as firm as she means them to be. "With you." It isn't in any archive. The door closes behind them.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Ione inclines her head, light holding steady. "I can wait," she says. "I have an excellent clock. Please do not make it too long."

anael.title: Lamplighter
anael.text: At dusk Anael walks the street with Sam, lighting lanterns with a touch of her fingers, her white wings folded neatly behind her and the flames blooming one by one in her wake. She tells him, plainly, that the old Lantern Stone burned for the first time in four centuries on the night he arrived, and that the Order sent her to find out why. "I have concluded," she says, "that it was you." Sam says that's absurd. "I know," says Anael, with a small, helpless smile. "I have run out of other explanations."

choices.label: "I'm glad it was me."
choices.res: Her wings relax a full inch, feathers rustling. "So am I," she says. "I find I am not objective about it." The next lantern lights before she touches it.

choices.label: Ask what happens when she finds out
choices.res: "I report," she says, fingers hovering over the next wick. A pause. "Or I do not. That part of the protocol has become unclear." The flame catches, wavering.

image.comp: walking along a street at dusk lighting lanterns with a touch of her fingertip, wings folded behind her, turning to him with a small smile
image.setting: lantern-lit cobbled street at dusk

anael.title: Not the Wings
anael.text: Sam opens the washroom door to find Anael perched on the edge of the tub, wings dripping onto the tiles, wrapped in a towel and a deep, full-body blush. Her halo has dimmed to a candle-glow in the steam. "The Order does not prepare one," she says with enormous dignity, "for the maintenance of plumage." She draws one wing in front of her like a shield. "Do not touch the wings. It is... impolite."

choices.label: Apologize and back out
choices.res: "Thank you," she says. "For the courtesy. It is noted." The note, as it turns out, is a very warm one, and arrives later that evening with a feather pressed between the pages.

choices.label: "Can I help dry them?"
choices.res: She holds very still while he blots the feathers with a towel, her breathing slow and careful. At the end her halo is brighter than the lamps.

else.res: "No," she says, rigid, wing clutched tighter. "Please leave." The wings snap shut with a thump, and a few droplets scatter across his hoodie.

choices.label: Offer her the soap
choices.res: She examines it, perplexed, turning it in her long fingers. "I have never required it," she admits. She keeps it anyway, and he finds it later on her windowsill.

image.comp: perched on the edge of a tub in a towel with dripping white wings drawn in front of her like a shield, blushing hard
image.setting: steamy wooden washroom

anael.title: Field Research: Pie
anael.text: Anael has decided to try human food in the name of research. She approaches a slice of berry pie as if it might be a trap, fork held like a surgical instrument, afternoon light slanting across her wings. After the first bite she goes completely still. After the second, her halo flickers. After the third, she looks Sam directly in the eye. "This changes my understanding of mortality," she says gravely. "Please do not tell the Order I enjoyed it so much."

choices.label: Stay with her
choices.res: He shares the pie. She feeds him a bite, solemnly, as though it were a sacrament, and purple juice stains her lip, and something warm settles over them both.

choices.label: Order a second slice
choices.res: She accepts with great composure and a gracious nod. She finishes it with considerably less, and eyes the plate afterward as though it had betrayed her.

image.comp: seated at a table with a slice of berry pie, eyes wide with solemn wonder, a soft glow flickering behind her head
image.setting: cozy inn lounge, afternoon light

anael.title: Recall
anael.text: A second angel, tall and stern, appears in the courtyard with a sealed scroll, the lamps flaring white at her presence. The Order has completed its review. Anael is recalled to the Quiet Lamp at the next new moon. She takes the scroll with perfect composure and tucks it into her sleeve, and the stern angel departs in a rush of feathers. That night Anael stands at Sam's door, wings drooping, one hand raised to knock, and does not knock.

choices.label: "Go, if it's your duty."
choices.res: "Duty," she repeats, and for the first time she sounds uncertain of the word. She does not leave, but she does not answer the scroll, either, and the halo flickers out in the hall.

choices.label: "Stay. Please."
choices.res: She reads her reply to the Order aloud. It is one line long. The messenger, a little scandalized, flies off before she can finish blushing.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.res: She waits, and then folds the scroll and bows, formal and distant. Her halo is dim for days, and the lanterns on the street burn low.

image.comp: standing outside his door at night holding a sealed scroll, wings drooping, uncertain, halo dim
image.setting: dim inn corridor at night, moonlight through a window

anael.title: Evensong
anael.text: In the chapel nook of the house, Anael sings the evensong of her order, a slow, ancient melody of lanterns and homecoming. Candlelight shivers on her wings, and the lights in the room rise and fall with her voice. Sam, who cannot sing, hums the bass line anyway, and the lanterns glow brighter in answer. She stops mid-verse, stares at him, and starts to laugh, helpless and bright, her halo flaring in delight.

choices.label: Keep humming
choices.res: They finish the evensong together, one voice shining and one decidedly flat. It is the best she has ever heard it, and she says so, tears on her cheeks.

choices.label: Listen in silence
choices.res: She sings the whole of it for him alone, golden eyes closed, and the room is warm for hours afterward, as though the walls remembered.

image.comp: standing in front of a small candlelit altar singing with wings half-spread, her halo glowing, glancing back at him with a delighted smile
image.setting: small candlelit chapel nook of an inn at night

anael.title: Report Withheld
anael.text: Anael finds Sam on the roof under the stars, the whole sleeping town laid out below them in lantern light. She opens her wings and then folds them around both of them, feathers warm and impossibly soft. "I have been asked to report on whether this soul is a danger to the world," she says. "I find that he is a danger only to my composure." She meets his eyes, golden and brave. "I would like to stay. Not as a Warden. As yourself." The door closes behind them.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Anael inclines her head, and her halo brightens, patient. "I can wait," she says. "The Order measures in centuries. Please do not make it quite so long."
